cues.text: One of the very earliest Church councils to survive in written form, gathered by nineteen bishops in southern Spain barely a year before persecution finally ended.
Its eighty-one canons offer an unusually candid snapshot of ordinary Christian life at the edge of the Roman world, regulating everything from mixed marriage to church attendance.
Among its most consequential rulings was an early formal requirement of celibacy for already-ordained clergy, a discipline that would shape Western priesthood for the rest of Church history.
Historians return to Elvira again and again as the clearest surviving window into how the pre-Constantinian Church actually governed itself.
